website-development.lede: Premium websites for manufacturers, exporters and B2B companies: written, designed and built to make you look as established as you are, and to turn serious buyers into enquiries.

It is shaped around how buyers check a supplier: they compare capabilities, look for proof of credibility and then send an enquiry or request a quote. WeberAct delivers it with a fixed scope, a fixed fee and a launch date agreed in writing.

website-development.cost_title: How much does B2B website development cost?
cost_text: The cost depends on the scope, not on a rate card. Every project has a fixed fee in a written proposal, in US dollars or your local currency, agreed before any work starts. The fee only changes if you ask for more, and any change is confirmed in writing first.
These are the things that change the scope most:
cost_factors: The number of pages and page templates
Custom features such as quote builders, catalogues or client portals
Integrations with your CRM, booking or other business tools
Whether we write the copy, and how much content needs moving from an old site
A redesign of an existing website, including redirects so search traffic is kept

faq.q: How long does it take to build a B2B website?
faq.a: Most projects take between two and eight weeks from the signed proposal, depending on the number of pages and any custom features. The launch date is written into the proposal before work starts.

faq.q: Can you redesign our website without losing search traffic?
faq.a: Yes. A redesign starts with a list of your current pages and the searches they already bring in. Every address that changes gets a permanent redirect, content that ranks is kept or improved, and we check Search Console for errors after launch.

faq.q: Will we be able to edit the website ourselves?
faq.a: Yes. You get an admin to edit pages and content, plus a walkthrough at handover. You can also ask us to make changes.

faq.q: Who owns the website?
faq.a: You do. The code, domain, hosting and accounts are in your name, with documentation at handover.

faq.q: What makes a manufacturing website generate enquiries?
faq.a: Buyers need to find the capability they are looking for quickly, trust that you can deliver it, and know how to ask for a quote. That means clear capability and product pages, proof such as certifications and project examples where you have them, fast pages on mobile, and a short quote form on every relevant page.

technical-seo.lede: Technical SEO, SEO audits and organic growth for manufacturers, exporters and B2B companies: so search engines and AI answer engines can find, understand and recommend your pages.
technical-seo.answer: Technical SEO is the work that lets search engines and AI answer engines find, crawl, understand and index a website. It covers site structure, speed, mobile usability, indexing, canonical addresses, structured data and internal links. It does not replace useful content; it makes sure useful content can be found and trusted.

cost_text: SEO is offered as a one-off audit or as a fixed monthly plan. Every project has a fixed fee in a written proposal, in US dollars or your local currency, agreed before any work starts. The fee only changes if you ask for more, and any change is confirmed in writing first.

faq.q: How long does SEO take to work?
faq.a: Fixes for serious technical problems, such as pages blocked from search or broken redirects, can show results soon after search engines recrawl the pages. Ranking for competitive commercial searches usually takes months rather than weeks, and depends on the competition, the site’s history and how much work goes in. We report progress every month, so you can see what is changing.

faq.q: How does technical SEO improve organic visibility?
faq.a: Search engines can only rank pages they can crawl, understand and index. Technical SEO removes what blocks that, such as broken links, duplicate pages, slow loading and missing structured data, so the content you already have can compete.

faq.q: What does a technical SEO audit include?
faq.a: Crawlability and indexing, sitemaps and robots rules, canonical addresses, redirects and broken links, duplicate and thin pages, mobile usability, Core Web Vitals, structured data, internal links and page titles and descriptions, each with a priority and a recommended fix.

faq.q: What should businesses look for in an SEO agency?
faq.a: A clear written scope, reporting on enquiries and not only on rankings, access to your own Search Console and analytics, methods that follow Google’s search guidelines, and no guaranteed rankings. Nobody can guarantee a position in Google.

faq.q: Do you guarantee rankings?
faq.a: No. Anyone who does is guessing. We do the technical and content work properly and report what changed every month.

faq.q: What business processes can be automated?
faq.a: Most repeated, rule-based work: replying to and qualifying enquiries, follow-ups, CRM updates, quote requests, invoices, order and stock updates, and reports. Work that needs judgement stays with your team, and the automation hands it to them.

faq.q: How can companies automate their lead generation?
faq.a: By connecting the channels where leads arrive to a workflow that replies instantly, asks qualifying questions, logs each lead in the CRM, assigns it to a person and follows up until the buyer responds. Outreach to new prospects can be automated too, within the email rules of each country.

faq.q: Will automation replace our sales team?
faq.a: No. It removes copying, pasting and waiting, so your team spends its time on conversations that need a person.

faq.q: Is customer data safe?
faq.a: Workflows run in accounts you own, access is limited to what each step needs, and personal data is only sent to an AI tool when that is necessary and agreed with you.

faq.q: How long does an automation project take?
faq.a: Most workflows take two to four weeks. WhatsApp automation also needs Meta’s approval, and larger AI assistant projects can take five to eight weeks. The timeline is written into the proposal.

faq.q: How can manufacturers generate international B2B leads?
faq.a: By combining three things: a website with clear capability pages and a short quote form, search visibility for the products and processes buyers search for, and targeted outreach to companies in each market. Each channel feeds the same qualification process, so your team only talks to buyers who fit.

faq.q: Is cold email to businesses legal in the US, UK, Canada, Australia and the UAE?
faq.a: It depends on the country. In the US, the CAN-SPAM Act covers business email too: it requires accurate sender details, a valid postal address and a working opt-out, which must be honoured promptly. In the UK, the PECR rules allow email to companies without prior consent if you identify yourself and offer an opt-out, while sole traders need consent. Canada’s CASL and Australia’s Spam Act require consent, which can be implied or inferred when a business publishes an address and the message relates to that person’s role. The UAE has its own personal data protection law. We check the rules for each campaign. This is general information, not legal advice.

faq.q: How long does it take to see results?
faq.a: New sending domains need two to three weeks of warm-up before campaigns run at full volume. After that, replies arrive as the sequences run, and targeting improves each month as we learn which companies and messages respond.

faq.q: How are leads qualified?
faq.a: Against criteria you set, such as country, company size, product need and timing. Replies that match are passed to your team with the context they need; the rest are logged and followed up or closed politely.

faq.q: Do you guarantee a number of leads or meetings?
faq.a: No. Results depend on the market, the offer and the list. We agree the activity and the reporting in writing, and report honestly on what it produces.

international.lede: How WeberAct works with B2B companies in the United States, United Kingdom, United Arab Emirates, Canada and Australia: remotely, in English, with everything agreed in writing.
international.answer_q: Does WeberAct work with businesses in the US, UK, UAE, Canada and Australia?
international.answer: Yes. WeberAct works remotely with B2B companies in these countries. Proposals, calls, progress updates and reports all happen online, in English, with fees in US dollars or your local currency. WeberAct has no offices in these countries, so the same team runs your project wherever you are.
international.who_title: What we plan for in each market

who.title: United States
who.text: US English spelling, and imperial units where your buyers use them. Business email follows the CAN-SPAM Act, and some states, such as California, have their own privacy laws.

who.title: United Kingdom
who.text: UK English spelling. Personal data falls under UK GDPR, email marketing under PECR, and analytics or marketing cookies need consent before they are set.

who.title: United Arab Emirates
who.text: Clear English pages for international and local buyers. Personal data falls under the UAE’s federal data protection law, and free zones such as DIFC and ADGM have their own data protection rules.

who.title: Canada
who.text: Canadian English spelling. Commercial email falls under CASL, which needs consent, and personal information under PIPEDA.

who.title: Australia
who.text: Australian English spelling. Commercial email falls under the Spam Act 2003, which needs consent, and personal information under the Privacy Act 1988.

international.cost_title: Should we have a separate website for each country?
cost_text: Only when it genuinely helps buyers. Separate country pages or sites make sense when products, prices, regulations or language differ between markets. When the offer is the same everywhere, one clear English website, with a page explaining how you serve international buyers, usually serves buyers and search engines better than near-duplicate country pages.
Country-specific pages are worth building when they have:
cost_factors: Different products, prices or delivery terms for that country
Different regulations, certifications or standards buyers must see
A different language, or local spelling and units that matter to buyers
Real local proof, such as projects or clients in that country

faq.q: Do you have offices in these countries?
faq.a: No. We work remotely with clients in these countries, and we do not claim a local office we do not have.

faq.q: Which currency do you invoice in?
faq.a: Proposals and invoices are in US dollars or your local currency, agreed in the proposal.

faq.q: How do meetings work across time zones?
faq.a: Calls are scheduled at a time that works for you, and progress is shared in writing between calls so nothing waits for a meeting.

faq.q: Can you help us win buyers in a new country?
faq.a: Yes. That usually combines a website that explains what you supply to that market, search visibility for what buyers there search for, and targeted outreach within that country’s email rules.
